concepts.def: Health: staying well, common illnesses and visiting the doctor, a core wellbeing topic.
Diet and eating habits, including healthy and unhealthy choices, e.g. 'gesund essen'.
Physical activity and exercise, and how regular sport benefits health and wellbeing.
Wellbeing, including mental health, stress and relaxation, and how to look after yourself.
Sleep and rest as part of a healthy lifestyle, e.g. getting enough hours each night.
Expressing obligation for healthy living, e.g. 'man muss Obst essen', with the infinitive at the end.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Theme 2: Lifestyle and Wellbeing — a core area of GCSE German.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Theme 2: Lifestyle and Wellbeing brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Theme 2: Lifestyle and Wellbeing.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Which sentence gives healthy-living advice correctly?
options: Man muss Obst und Gemüse essen.
Man muss isst Obst.
Man muss zu essen Obst.
Man muss Obst essen man.
To eat healthily
To skip meals
To eat only sweets
To cook professionally
Wellbeing
A bank
A stadium
Homework

mcqs.q: Which is part of a healthy lifestyle?
options: Regelmäßig Sport treiben
Jeden Tag rauchen
Nie schlafen
Zu viel Zucker essen

mcqs.q: How do you give advice with 'man muss'?
options: 'Man muss' + infinitive at the end, e.g. 'man muss Obst essen'
'Man muss zu essen'
To eat only sweets
'Man muss' + the 'ich' form
